verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/planner.py:127 (bare r'\?\s*$' in _READ_SIGNALS) + planner.py:135 (_AGENT_REQUEST_CUE exempts the '?' only for r'\b(can|could|would|will) you\b|\bplease\b') + planner.py:230-236 — every other agent-addressed question ('Any chance you could…', 'Do you mind…', 'Mind noting…', 'Think you could…', 'Is it alright if you…') with no listed edit verb gets the '?' as its only signal, so sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1803 (read_only = inferred_intent == 'read' and bool(intent.signals)) strips every data write at :1807-1829.
verdicts.fix_shape: In classify_intent, stop treating the bare trailing '?' as a positive read cue by default: count it only when the text opens with an interrogative from a closed set (is/are/am/was/were/do/does/did/has/have/had/how/what/which/who/whom/whose/when/where/why) that is not immediately a request frame (followed by you/you'd/if/it (be) ok|okay|alright|possible|fine); keep the existing can/could/would/will-you and please exemptions. This closes the class by enumerating the closed interrogative set instead of the open set of request frames (no fourth round of phrase-adding). A question that does not open with an interrogative then counts as cue-less and keeps the full set per D-B3-3; data writes still stage for review. Simulated at HEAD through the real invoke_agent: 43/43 write asks keep their tool (9 strip at HEAD), and 12/12 real-read controls still strip (the 13th, 'Are markets open today?', keeps writes at HEAD through the pre-existing \bopen\b edit cue, unchanged).
